mainText: This is Dose of Good for Sunday, November 8. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Indigenous and quilombola diplomats join Brazil's foreign service for the first time. Marcelo Kariri Meneses, Idjahure Achkar Terena and quilombola Helen Jaine Borgens, 25, are part of a new class of 60 diplomats, 45% of them women. Second: 5-year-old Brazilian girl wins gold at an international maths olympiad. Pietra Garcia, from Bahia, won the K2 category at an olympiad in Singapore. It is her 14th medal; she won bronze at age 4. Third: Whale and calf swim up to a woman singing in the sea. Artist Demetra was singing in the water when an adult whale and a calf appeared close by. The video moved many online; there is no proof the song drew them in. Fourth: Councillor uses an AirTag to catch a thief stealing 18th-century stones. Matt Smith hid an AirTag in a capstone of an 18th-century wall in Rufford, England. The thief was arrested and convicted, and some of the roughly 30 stones were recovered. Fifth: Family Doberman detects a baby's racing heartbeat and helps save him. Saraya kept insisting something was wrong with 6-month-old Alexander, whose heart was beating at 280 bpm. He was diagnosed with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome and treated. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
